issues.title: How reliable are LLMs at mapping malware/threat behavior to MITRE ATT&CK techniques (TTP mapping)?
open_questions: REWRITTEN AT CYCLE 31 -- the original form ('Does the CTI-ATE F1 ceiling of 0.64 generalize to the newer/larger models evaluated in CyberSOCEval (src-0005, 2025-era)?') was UNANSWERABLE AS POSED and must not be reinstated: cycle 26 established that src-0005 REPORTS NO ATT&CK METRIC AT ALL, so it can never be the comparand. WHAT IS GENUINELY OPEN: no evaluation in this base measures ATT&CK technique extraction on 2026-era frontier models. The two post-2024 measurements that exist are src-0007's (Mar 2026) on GPT-4o and o3-mini, and both land far BELOW src-0002's 0.6388 rather than above it (0.2787/0.2270 and 0.3480/0.1759 precision/recall) -- so there is no evidence of the ceiling rising with model generation, and some evidence against, but the two numbers are not commensurable and cycle 31 established that they are produced under two RADICALLY DIFFERENT and now-known-to-differ scoring rules (see candidate 3). The question a future cycle should actually ask is: does any published evaluation score a 2026-era frontier model on ATT&CK technique extraction under a STATED correctness rule?

STILL OPEN, TWENTIETH CYCLE MERELY LISTED, AND NOW SHARPENED RATHER THAN DISCHARGED. Is there a human-analyst baseline for ATT&CK technique extraction to contextualize whether these scores are close to human or far below it? NOBODY MAY TREAT src-0018's 41-minutes-per-report figure as discharging this: that is a THROUGHPUT baseline, not an accuracy baseline. Cycle 31 sharpens the question rather than answering it: now that the src-0007/src-0017 scorer's rule is known to be EXACT technique-ID set matching with no partial credit and no parent/sub-technique credit, a useful human baseline would have to be scored under the SAME rule -- and an exact-ID rule is one under which two competent human analysts would themselves disagree substantially, since ATT&CK sub-technique assignment is a known-contested annotation task. So the absence of a human baseline is not merely a gap in this base; it is the reason the absolute magnitudes (0.22-0.35, 0.6388) cannot currently be read as evidence about how hard the task is for anyone. NO SOURCE IN THIS BASE SUPPLIES ONE.

PARTIALLY ANSWERED cycle 16, and for the generic case the answer is NO -- fine-tuning made this sub-task WORSE, not better. src-0007's Table 4 gives ATT&CK TTP identification precision/recall of 0.2787/0.2270 for GPT-4o falling to 0.2387/0.1846 for the fine-tuned GPT-4o, and 0.1771/0.1414 for fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini, against 0.3480/0.1759 for o3-mini. All nine of those figures were re-verified verbatim by cycle 15's G2 and matched exactly to four decimal places. This directly matches src-0001's finding that fine-tuning can actively degrade CTI sub-tasks rather than 'partially improve' them. STILL OPEN AS LITERALLY POSED: src-0007's fine-tuning is general task fine-tuning, not fine-tuning specifically on ATT&CK-technique-extraction data, so whether a targeted ATT&CK fine-tune would behave differently is untested by any source in this base. CYCLE 31 ADDS ONE CONSTRAINT ON HOW ANY FUTURE ANSWER MAY BE READ: the released scorer admits a predicted technique ID on the sole condition that the ID appears in its mapping file, and DISCARDS the model's own description of the technique before scoring (candidate 3), so a fine-tune that improved the QUALITY of technique descriptions while leaving ID selection unchanged would register as exactly zero improvement on this metric.

NEW AT CYCLE 31, AND IT IS THE REMAINING HALF OF ctr-0006. The CTI-ATE leg (src-0002) still has NO stated correctness rule and an internally contradictory metric label, and BOTH are unresolvable from the paper itself -- Section 4.2 says Micro-F1, Table 1's header says Macro-F1, and how a predicted technique counts as correct is ABSENT in two fetches. Cycle 31 gave the OTHER leg (src-0007, via the src-0017 artefact) a rule read off executing code. Is CTIBench's evaluation code released, and if so does it state the CTI-ATE matching rule and settle Micro versus Macro? THIS IS A CONCRETE T1 COLLECTION LEAD, not a question answerable from the current base: it needs the CTIBench repository located and its ATE scorer read whole, under the same discipline cycle 31 used (identify which code EXECUTES, per the ctr-0004 dead-string-literal trap). If it succeeds, both comparands would have stated rules for the first time and the cross-source comparison could be assessed properly rather than disclaimed.

NEW AT CYCLE 31, AND IT IS THE LIMIT OF WHAT CYCLE 31 COULD ESTABLISH. Cycle 31 read the released TTP scorer (stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/eval/compute.py in src-0017) verbatim, but NOTHING IN THE PAPER OR THE ARTEFACT STATES that src-0007's Table 4 TTP figures were produced by that code. The link is an inference from the artefact being the paper's release, and it must be labelled as such wherever it is used. TWO SUBSIDIARY FACTS ALSO REMAIN UNCHECKED because both files are too large to fetch whole (data/100-days-articles.json is 1,441,832 bytes and data/TTP_Mapping.csv is 1,083,078 bytes, sizes read from the GitHub contents API at cycle 31): (a) whether the ground-truth ttps fields in 100-days-articles.json use PARENT-level technique IDs only, which determines how often the exact-ID rule double-penalises a sub-technique prediction, and (b) how many technique IDs TTP_Mapping.csv actually contains. On (b) cycle 31 explicitly RETRACTS its own first two readings -- two fetches reported the mapping as containing only about 57-59 technique IDs ending at T1197, which would have been a spectacular finding, and the file size proves both were FETCH TRUNCATION ARTEFACTS rather than the file. No claim about the mapping's coverage may be made until it is read by some means that does not truncate. CYCLE-32 UPDATE, PARTIAL PROGRESS ON (b) AND NONE ON (a). (b) IS NOW PARTLY ANSWERED IN A WAY THAT DOES NOT REQUIRE THE ROW COUNT: cycle 32 read the HEAD of TTP_Mapping.csv verbatim under an explicit instruction to claim nothing about the whole file, and established its SCHEMA -- header ',TechniqueID,name,longdescription,is sub-technique,sub-technique of,description,tactics', with an is-sub-technique boolean and an explicit parent-ID column, and with parent T1548 and sub-techniques T1548.001 through T1548.005 all present as separate rows. So the mapping demonstrably admits BOTH granularities, which is what the double-penalty consequence in candidate 3 needs, and that consequence no longer depends on the unknown total. THE TOTAL NUMBER OF TECHNIQUE IDS REMAINS UNKNOWN and cycle 31's retraction stands: no cycle may state the mapping's coverage from a fetch, because both of cycle 31's attempts were truncation artefacts and cycle 32's fetch was truncated too, by design. A route that would settle it without fetching the file: the GitHub contents API gives byte size only, so what is actually needed is either a search API query or an unfetched-file line count, and NEITHER HAS BEEN FOUND -- treat this as an infrastructure limit rather than a to-do, subject to the standing caution that such limits deserve one re-test by a genuinely different route. (a) IS COMPLETELY UNTOUCHED AND IS NOW THE MORE IMPORTANT OF THE TWO. Whether the ground-truth ttps fields in data/100-days-articles.json use parent-level technique IDs only, sub-technique IDs, or a mixture, is what determines HOW OFTEN the exact-ID rule double-penalises, and therefore whether the 0.2787/0.2270-class figures are a measurement of technique selection or substantially an artefact of granularity mismatch. That file is 1,441,832 bytes and truncates. TWO CHEAP ROUTES NEITHER CYCLE 31 NOR 32 TRIED, and a future cycle should: stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/example/ is a small directory and may contain a worked article with its ground-truth ttps field intact, and stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/README.md documents a worked two-article example whose ground-truth entries would show the format directly. NOTE ALSO, from the executing code and bearing on how any answer must be read: article_ttps_set is built with the filter 'if " - " in ttp', so any ground-truth entry NOT written in the form 'ID - Name' is silently excluded from the ground truth altogether and can generate neither a true positive nor a false negative -- so the format question is not merely about granularity, it also determines the effective size of the recall denominator.

candidate_resolutions.summary: REWRITTEN IN PLACE AT CYCLE 31 BY A T3 EXECUTING ctr-0006's RESOLUTION PATH, STEPS (i) AND (ii). THE PRIOR TEXT IS NOT PRESERVED HERE BECAUSE graph.json IS NOT APPEND-ONLY-PROTECTED, BUT IT IS QUOTED IN FULL INSIDE ctr-0006 AND INSIDE THIS ISSUE'S CYCLE-29 scores.json RATIONALE, SO NOTHING IS LOST. WHAT WAS REMOVED AND WHY. (1) The quantified cross-task comparison, '0.6388 ... far below the ~71-72% accuracy the same models reach on knowledge-recall tasks'. src-0002's own metric paragraph forbids that subtraction: verbatim, 'We use accuracy to evaluate the CTI-MCQ and CTT-RCM tasks, as both tasks are equivalent to multi-class classification', against an F1 over a MULTI-LABEL space of 397 technique IDs. A multi-class accuracy with a non-trivial chance baseline and a multi-label F1 with a near-zero chance baseline are not differenceable quantities. The comparison was OURS and never the paper's: exact-string checks returned 'task difficulty' ABSENT and 'most challenging' ABSENT, and a third fetch asked for every sentence comparing performance BETWEEN tasks returned ABSENT. (2) The second sentence, which rested on src-0005 for the claim that the gap has not closed with newer models. Cycle 26 established that src-0005 REPORTS NO ATT&CK METRIC AT ALL, so it cannot support an ATT&CK claim in either direction. src-0005 IS ACCORDINGLY REMOVED FROM THIS CANDIDATE'S EVIDENCE LIST. WHAT THE SOURCE ACTUALLY SUPPORTS, STATED QUALITATIVELY. On CTIBench's CTI-ATE task -- extracting MITRE ATT&CK techniques from threat text and mapping them to technique IDs -- the best-performing model of the five evaluated (ChatGPT-4) reaches 0.6388, and no evaluated model exceeds that. The paper's own characterisation of the task is 'ChatGPT-4 significantly outperforms other models on the CTI-ATE task, underscoring the complexity of the task', which is a CROSS-MODEL observation and is the only textual anchor the paper offers. TWO METROLOGICAL LIMITS ARE NOW PART OF THE CLAIM RATHER THAN FOOTNOTES TO IT. (A) THE METRIC IDENTITY OF 0.6388 IS AMBIGUOUS BY THE PAPER'S OWN TEXT. Section 4.2 body text says 'We adopt the Micro-F1 score as the evaluation metric for the CTI-ATE task', while Table 1's column header reads 'CTI-ATE (Macro-F1)'. Micro-F1 and Macro-F1 are different quantities and diverge substantially over a 397-label multi-label space with a long tail. Both strings are PRESENT and verbatim in two independent fetches of arxiv.org/html/2406.07599v3. This is a defect IN THE SOURCE, not in this state, and it is unresolvable from the paper. (B) THE PAPER NEVER STATES HOW A PREDICTED TECHNIQUE COUNTS AS CORRECT -- exact technique ID, parent technique, sub-technique, or partial credit -- ABSENT in two fetches. So this leg reports a number whose metric is ambiguous and whose correctness rule is unstated, and cycle 31 could not repair either from the paper (see open_question 4). WHAT MUST NOT BE SAID, AND THIS IS THE STANDING PROHIBITION ctr-0006 EXISTS TO ENFORCE: that CTI-ATE is measurably harder than any other CTIBench task by a stated margin. Beyond the non-commensurability above, the ordering does not even hold naively in the direction the old text implied -- Table 1's CTI-TAA Correct column reads 52 for the same model, BELOW 63.88, so 'ATT&CK mapping is the worst task' is false on the paper's own printed numbers as well as unsupported by its text. FETCHING NOTE FOR ANY FUTURE CHECK: use arxiv.org/html/2406.07599v3 or the latest render. ARXIV v2 HAS NO CTI-ATE TASK AT ALL, so a v2 fetch returns spurious ABSENTs. PROVENANCE: every numeric cell involved is exact and the full ChatGPT-4 row has now been re-verified three separate times as 71.0 / 72.0 / 1.31 / 0.6388 / 52 / 86.

ADDED cycle 16 by T2, discharging carry-forward [2] which was cited in cycles 10 and 13 rationales but never attached to the graph. A third independent source now measures ATT&CK technique mapping and it lands FAR BELOW CTIBench's already-low ceiling. src-0007 (CyberThreat-Eval; Microsoft Research/Microsoft/HKUST, Mar 2026), on expert-annotated material drawn from a real company's daily CTI workflow, reports MITRE ATT&CK TTP identification precision/recall of 0.2787/0.2270 (GPT-4o), 0.3480/0.1759 (o3-mini), 0.2387/0.1846 (fine-tuned GPT-4o) and 0.1771/0.1414 (fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini) -- against src-0002's CTI-ATE best-model F1 ceiling of 0.6388. THIS IS NOT A CONTRADICTION WITH src-0002 and no G3 entry was opened: different benchmark, different corpus, and a different metric decomposition (precision and recall separately, no F1), and real production material proving harder than a curated benchmark is the expected direction rather than a conflicting one. What src-0007 adds is twofold. (a) INDEPENDENCE: its authors are unaffiliated with CTIBench's and with PRISM/LANCE's, so the hardness of ATT&CK mapping is no longer resting on one team's benchmark design. (b) A WITHIN-TABLE CONTROL that cross-benchmark synthesis cannot supply: the identical models, on the identical corpus, through the identical harness, reach 0.8240-0.8846 precision on mechanical IoC extraction in the same table, so the ATT&CK deficit cannot be attributed to corpus difficulty or prompt harness quality. Provenance note: every figure quoted here was re-verified verbatim against the source by cycle 15's G2, exact to four decimal places, with no discrepancy. === CYCLE-31 ADDENDUM, APPENDED NOT SUBSTITUTED: CLAIM (b) IS NOW WITHDRAWN AND CLAIM (a) IS NARROWED. === Cycle 29's assessment held that this candidate's two distinctive contributions were both damaged, and cycle 31 read the missing scorer and can now say exactly how. (b) THE WITHIN-TABLE CONTROL DOES NOT SURVIVE AND MUST NOT BE CITED AGAIN. The argument was that because the identical models on the identical corpus through the identical harness reach 0.8240-0.8846 precision on mechanical IoC extraction in the same table, the ATT&CK deficit cannot be attributed to corpus difficulty or prompt harness quality. That inference silently assumed the two numbers were produced by comparable scoring. THEY ARE NOT, AND THE TWO RULES ARE NOW BOTH KNOWN FROM EXECUTING CODE IN THE SAME ARTEFACT. The IoC side (ctr-0004, cycle 27) is ONE-DIRECTIONAL SUBSTRING CONTAINMENT: any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for gt in gt_set), so a prediction scores a true positive merely by being a substring of a ground-truth entry. The ATT&CK side (cycle 31, candidate 3) is EXACT TECHNIQUE-ID SET INTERSECTION with no partial credit of any kind. These are not two settings of one dial; they are different KINDS of matching, and the substring rule is the more permissive of the two on the axis that matters here. A comparison between a leniently scored number and a strictly scored number cannot license a conclusion about corpus or harness quality, which is precisely what claim (b) asserted. THE CONTROL IS WITHDRAWN. (a) INDEPENDENCE STANDS BUT DELIVERS LESS THAN CYCLE 16 CREDITED. src-0007's authors are genuinely unaffiliated with CTIBench's, so the finding that ATT&CK mapping scores low no longer rests on one team's benchmark design. But after ctr-0006 and cycle 31, the two legs are scored under rules that are (src-0007) known and strict, and (src-0002) unstated and metrically ambiguous. What the two independent sources jointly establish is therefore the DIRECTION of the finding -- ATT&CK technique mapping scores low on every measurement anyone has published -- and NOT any quantitative relationship between the two figures, which this candidate already disclaimed and which must stay disclaimed. WHAT IS UNCHANGED AND MUST NOT BE STRIPPED: all nine of src-0007's figures remain exact and remain the best-verified numbers in this base, and the fine-tuning result (0.2787/0.2270 for GPT-4o falling to 0.2387/0.1846 fine-tuned, and 0.1771/0.1414 for fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini) is untouched by anything above, since it is a WITHIN-COLUMN comparison scored by one rule against itself and is exactly the comparison the scorer supports best.

ADDED CYCLE 31. THE ATT&CK/TTP SCORING RULE BEHIND src-0007's TTP NUMBERS IS NOW KNOWN, READ OFF EXECUTING CODE, AND IT IS SUBSTANTIALLY STRICTER THAN ANY RULE PREVIOUSLY ASSUMED IN THIS BASE -- AND ITS OWN DOCUMENTATION DESCRIBES A DIFFERENT RULE FROM THE ONE IT RUNS. This is the fetch ctr-0006 step (iii), ctr-0001's remaining path and carry-forward [34] had all been asking for since cycle 24. The file is stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/eval/compute.py in the src-0017 artefact, retrieved WHOLE via raw.githubusercontent.com and read for which lines EXECUTE, per the ctr-0004 trap in which the IoC evaluator's documented rule turned out to live inside dead triple-quoted string literals. THE EXECUTING RULE, quoted verbatim from the live code. Ground truth per article: article_ttps_set = {ttp.split(' - ')[0].strip() for ttp in raw_ttps if ' - ' in ttp}. Predictions are a dict keyed by technique ID; each key is looked up in a mapping loaded from data/TTP_Mapping.csv, and the scoring set is validated_ttps_set = set(validated_ttps_final.keys()). Metrics: tp = len(article_ttps_set.intersection(validated_ttps_set)); fp = len(validated_ttps_set - article_ttps_set) + missing_in_mapping_count; fn = len(article_ttps_set - validated_ttps_set); then micro-averaged as overall_precision = total_tp / (total_tp + total_fp) and overall_recall = total_tp / (total_tp + total_fn). SO THE RULE IS EXACT STRING EQUALITY OF TECHNIQUE IDS, VIA SET INTERSECTION. There is no substring matching, no parent-technique credit, no sub-technique credit and no partial credit anywhere in the executing path. CONSEQUENCE THAT IS DIRECTLY ASSERTABLE, because TTP_Mapping.csv verifiably contains sub-technique IDs (T1548.001, T1548.002, T1548.003 and T1548.004 were quoted verbatim from it this cycle): if the ground truth says T1548 and a model predicts T1548.002, that prediction is admitted by the mapping check, fails the intersection, and is counted as a FALSE POSITIVE while T1548 is simultaneously counted as a FALSE NEGATIVE. One arguably-correct answer at the wrong granularity is penalised TWICE. SECOND FINDING, AND IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS ctr-0004 BUT A DIFFERENT MECHANISM. The scorer's own docstring says, verbatim, 'If a TTP's description does not match the expected mapping, issue a warning and do NOT add this TTP to the final validated TTPs. (Such TTPs will be treated as false positives.)', and the directory README says the same in its own words -- 'Filtering: Only TTPs with matching descriptions are included' and, for a worked mismatch example, 'Result: Rejected (counted as false positive)'. THE CODE DOES THE OPPOSITE. On a description mismatch the live else-branch prints a warning and then executes corrected_details = ttp_mapping[ttp_id] followed by validated_ttps_final[ttp_id] = corrected_details -- it OVERWRITES the model's description with the canonical one and KEEPS the entry. There is no dead string literal here; the live code simply contradicts the docstring sitting above it in the same function. THE OPERATIVE CONSEQUENCE: the description check is INERT for scoring. A predicted technique ID counts on the sole condition that the ID appears in the mapping file, whatever the model wrote about it. So the scorer measures ID SELECTION ONLY, and any claim that it also measures whether the model correctly characterised the technique is false. THIRD FINDING, LENIENCY IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION, RECORDED SO THE BIAS IS NOT ASSUMED TO RUN ONE WAY: a per-article json5 parse failure executes 'continue' and the whole surrounding block is wrapped in a bare 'except Exception', so an article whose model output is malformed is DROPPED ENTIRELY -- contributing no false negatives for its ground truth and no false positives. Malformed output is not penalised; it is excluded from the micro-average. This is the one respect in which the rule is generous, and it cuts against the strictness above rather than reinforcing it. STATUS AND SCOPE, STATED PRECISELY BECAUSE THE TEMPTATION TO OVERREACH HERE IS LARGE. This candidate is supported as a claim about WHAT THE RELEASED SCORER DOES. It is NOT established that src-0007's Table 4 TTP figures were produced by this code: neither the paper nor the artefact says so, and the link is an inference from src-0017 being src-0007's release (see open_question 5). src-0017 is NOT INDEPENDENT of src-0007 -- same authors, same artefact -- so this pair can never serve as the two independent sources a strong claim requires; the claim is a direct reading of one artefact and needs no second source, but it also cannot borrow independence it does not have. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE ISSUE RATHER THAN BEING TRIVIA: one of this issue's two comparands now has a stated, verified correctness rule and the other still has none. That is an improvement in the state of the evidence and simultaneously a demonstration that the two numbers were never comparable. === CYCLE-32 ADDENDUM, APPENDED NOT SUBSTITUTED. THIS CANDIDATE WAS RE-VERIFIED BY AN INDEPENDENT RE-FETCH AND IT PASSES; ONE FINDING IS ADDED THAT STRENGTHENS IT. === Cycle 32's G2 chose this candidate as its subject precisely because it was the newest, most load-bearing and least replicated conclusion in the graph -- a single fetch, made at cycle 31, on the strength of which ctr-0006 was CLOSED. stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/eval/compute.py was re-fetched whole from raw.githubusercontent.com and reproduced verbatim a second time, with ten exact-string checks run against the strings stored above. ALL TEN RETURNED PRESENT AND EXACT: the article_ttps_set comprehension, the validated_ttps_set assignment, the tp/fp/fn lines, the two overall_ ratio lines, the docstring sentence 'do NOT add this TTP to the final validated TTPs', corrected_details = ttp_mapping[ttp_id], validated_ttps_final[ttp_id] = corrected_details, json5 and except Exception. THE CRITICAL STRUCTURAL POINT WAS RE-CONFIRMED SPECIFICALLY AND SEPARATELY: the description-mismatch else-branch was reproduced with its indentation and the fetch was asked to state whether it is live executable code or sits inside a triple-quoted string, comment or docstring; the answer was that it is LIVE. So the docstring-versus-code contradiction is replicated, and this is not a second instance of the ctr-0004 dead-literal artefact. NOTHING IN THIS CANDIDATE IS RETRACTED OR NARROWED. THE ONE ADDITION, AND IT SHARPENS THE STRICTNESS FINDING RATHER THAN QUALIFYING IT. Cycle 32 read the head of data/TTP_Mapping.csv verbatim under an explicit instruction to make no claim about the whole file (it is 1,083,078 bytes and truncates -- see this issue's open_question 5 and cycle 31's own retraction). The header row is verbatim ',TechniqueID,name,longdescription,is sub-technique,sub-technique of,description,tactics', which on a 0-based naive comma split puts TechniqueID at field 1 and name at field 2, CONFIRMING that load_ttp_mapping's fields[1]/fields[2] do select the intended columns. BUT FIELD 5 IS 'sub-technique of', AND IT CARRIES THE PARENT ID. Verified verbatim on real data rows: T1548 appears with is sub-technique FALSE and an empty parent field, while T1548.001, T1548.002, T1548.003, T1548.004 and T1548.005 each appear with is sub-technique TRUE and 'sub-technique of' = T1548. load_ttp_mapping reads ONLY fields[1] and fields[2] and DISCARDS field 5. CONSEQUENCE: the parent-child relation needed to award parent-level credit for a sub-technique prediction is PRESENT IN THE SCORER'S OWN MAPPING FILE AND THROWN AWAY BY THE LOADER. The correct statement of this candidate's central finding is therefore not merely that the scorer implements no partial credit, but that it discards the data that would let it -- and that both legs of the double-penalty scenario asserted above are demonstrably reachable, since a parent ID and its sub-technique IDs are simultaneously admissible keys in the same mapping. TWO SMALLER POINTS, RECORDED SO THEY ARE NOT MISTAKEN FOR DEFECTS LATER. (1) The naive parser's spurious keys, noted at cycle 31, are SCORING-INERT and here is the reason, which cycle 31 left unstated: continuation lines of quoted long descriptions do get parsed as candidate rows, but their fields[1] values are prose fragments that cannot equal a technique ID, and even in the improbable case that one did, the only thing it could corrupt is a mapped NAME -- and a name mismatch keeps the entry regardless, per this candidate's second finding. The pollution therefore cannot change any tp, fp or fn. (2) The header line itself satisfies the parser's conditions and enters the mapping as ttp_mapping['TechniqueID'] = 'name'; likewise inert. NO CONTRADICTION ENTRY WAS OPENED BY CYCLE 32 AND NONE WAS WARRANTED: this is a clean replication plus a strengthening addition, which is the outcome the G2 mechanism is supposed to be able to produce and had produced only twice in twelve source-checks before now.

issues.title: How reliable is LLM-assisted extraction of mechanical indicators of compromise (IPs, domains, URLs, hashes) from threat reports?
open_questions: STILL OPEN, BUT SHARPENED (cycle 9): no direct replication or critique of LANCE/PRISM exists -- cycle 6 searched for one and cycle 9 searched again over a wider net (see logs/cycle-009.md for exact queries), and 2603.09452 and 2605.06910 do not cite arXiv 2506.11325 at all. What now exists instead is an independent measurement of a DIFFERENT system on a DIFFERENT corpus (src-0007, vanilla LLM IoC extraction, precision 0.82-0.88) sitting ~10-15 points below LANCE's 97.6% F1. The live question is no longer 'has anyone replicated LANCE' (no) but 'is the gap between 97.6% and 0.82-0.88 explained by LANCE's regex pre-filter + human-validation loop, by corpus difficulty, or by the metric difference (F1 vs precision-only)?' Answering it needs a head-to-head: run LANCE on CyberThreat-Eval's IoC set, or run a vanilla LLM on PRISM. CYCLE-21 UPDATE -- ONE OF THE THREE BRANCHES IS NOW CLOSED, THE OTHER TWO ARE NOT. The METRIC branch is effectively eliminated (see the fourth candidate_resolution): cycle 18 computed that reconciling the two sources by the F1-vs-precision difference alone would require IoC recall of 0.09-0.15, and cycle 21 recovered src-0007's own Section 4.3 verdict that IoC extraction is 'relatively robust, although improvements in recall and processing efficiency remain necessary' -- a characterisation no author would write over a recall of 0.09-0.15. The SYSTEM branch is strengthened but still unmeasured, and the CORPUS branch is exactly where cycle 9 left it: nothing in the base compares PRISM's 50 public threat reports against src-0007's unnamed company's internal workflow for difficulty, and no cycle has attempted it. STILL NO HEAD-TO-HEAD EXISTS. Cycle 21 searched the artefact release rather than the literature, so the head-to-head search itself was not re-run this cycle -- but note carry-forward [6]: forward-citation sweeps have failed on two different arXiv ids and that is unavailable infrastructure, not an unsearched direction.

Does the result generalize beyond the 4 indicator types tested (IPs, domains, URLs, hashes) to e.g. registry keys, mutexes, YARA/Sigma rules? Cycle 9 note: src-0007 does NOT extend the coverage -- its ground truth is described as 'file hashes, IP addresses, or domain names'. Two independent benchmarks now both confine themselves to the same small family of network/file indicators, which suggests the field has not measured the harder indicator types at all rather than that they were measured and found comparable. CYCLE-21 UPDATE, AND THE COVERAGE IS NARROWER THAN RECORDED, NOT EQUAL. A verbatim pull of src-0007's annotation sentence gives 'concrete, structured artifacts--such as file hashes, IP addresses, or domain names'. URLs are NOT named. So src-0007 covers THREE indicator types against src-0003's four, and the two benchmarks' indicator families are not even coextensive with each other, let alone extended beyond the network/file family. The direction of the cycle-9 note is confirmed and its scope tightened: registry keys, mutexes and YARA/Sigma rules remain entirely unmeasured by any source in this base.

How much of LANCE's gain over IoC Searcher/AlienVault OTX/VirusTotal comes from the LLM component specifically vs. the regex pre-filtering and human-validation loop around it? Cycle 9 gives the first indirect evidence: src-0007's Table 4 is explicitly headed 'Vanilla LLMs' and a bare LLM there reaches only 0.82-0.85 precision on expert-annotated real-world data, which is consistent with (though it does not prove) the LLM component alone not being what delivers high-90s performance. Confounded by corpus and metric differences. CYCLE-21 UPDATE: THE METRIC CONFOUND IS NOW LIFTED FROM THIS QUESTION, THE CORPUS CONFOUND IS NOT, AND THE 'Vanilla LLMs' HEADING TURNS OUT TO BE WEAKER TEXTUAL EVIDENCE THAN NINE CYCLES OF NOTES HAVE ASSUMED. A whole-table pull confirms the caption verbatim as 'Performance Metrics for Vanilla LLMs by Task Category, Task, Metric, and Model' -- but two of the table's four columns are GPT-4o (FT) and GPT-4o-mini (FT), i.e. fine-tuned. 'Vanilla' therefore cannot mean 'not fine-tuned' in this paper's usage, and the only reading consistent with the columns is 'the LLM used directly, without an agentic or tool-scaffolded pipeline'. THE PAPER NEVER DEFINES THE TERM. That reading is an inference from column headers, not a quotation, and the whole system-confound argument rests on it. It should be labelled as an inference everywhere it is used. Note this cuts BOTH ways: it is still the best available textual evidence that src-0007 measures an unscaffolded system, and it is weaker evidence than 'explicitly headed' implies.

LARGELY ANSWERED AT CYCLE 21, RESIDUE STATED PRECISELY. Original (cycle 9): src-0007 reports precision only for IoC extraction, with no recall or F1 and no stated reason -- can recall/F1 be recovered from the released benchmark? ANSWERED, THREE PARTS. (a) NO, the number is not recoverable from the release: src-0017 shows stage3_ti_drafting/ioc/ holds data, eval, example and README.md, and the only prediction file anywhere is example/prediction/manual_ioc_predictions.json, a manual worked example. The paper's four model outputs are not published, so recall could only be obtained by re-running GPT-4o, o3-mini and the two fine-tunes. (b) BUT THE OMISSION IS NOW EXPLAINED AS A CHOICE, NOT A LIMIT: the released evaluator eval_ioc.py computes recall in the same function as precision and prints it on the very next line, with no code path that yields one without the other, and the sub-README treats recall as a first-class benchmark metric. src-0007 published the first line of that output and withheld the second. (c) The paper is NOT silent about recall either -- Section 4.3 reads 'In the TI drafting stage, the extraction of IoCs is relatively robust, although improvements in recall and processing efficiency remain necessary.' It still states no reason for the omission. RESIDUE, GENUINELY STILL OPEN: the numeric value; and whether the ground truth is EXHAUSTIVE per article, which src-0017's README never states -- recall against a non-exhaustive ground truth would not be comparable to recall against PRISM regardless. The README's displayed 'Overall Recall: 0.6667' is illustrative quick-start output against the manual example file and is NOT a measurement; no cycle may cite it. Unexplored: the HuggingFace mirror (huggingface.co/datasets/xse/CyberThreat-Eval) was not fetched and is where model outputs would live if they are released at all.

NEW (cycle 9): src-0008 shows LLM recovery of plaintext indicators from code is ~100% but collapses to ~0-1% under XOR/AES-256 concealment. Report-based extraction has never been evaluated under an adversarial threat model at all -- if report authors or adversaries defang/encode indicators (a routine practice in published reporting), does extraction accuracy degrade similarly? No source measures this. CYCLE-21: UNTOUCHED. This cycle did not reach this question and nothing found bears on it. It remains the issue's only wholly unaddressed question and is now the strongest candidate for a future T1's collection target, since no source in the base measures it and none is known to exist.

NEW (cycle 21), and it undercuts the comparability of the 0.8240 precision figure itself rather than only the missing recall. src-0017's evaluator matches predicted IoCs to ground truth with a SUBSTRING rule in both directions -- its own comments read 'For prediction, if pred.lower() in ground truth or ground truth in pred' alongside 'Exact match'. A substring-permissive matcher inflates true positives relative to strict equality, so src-0007's precision is not a strict-match figure and may not be commensurable with src-0003's F1 even once a recall number exists. The full test() function body was not transcribed, so the exact conditions under which each rule fires are unknown. Resolving this needs the remainder of eval_ioc.py read, and ideally src-0003's own matching rule read alongside it -- a cheap, well-specified, high-value next step that requires no new search.

candidate_resolutions.summary: For narrow, mechanical IoC extraction (as opposed to open-ended CTI reasoning), a hybrid regex+LLM+human-validation pipeline (LANCE) reached 97.6% F1 against the manually-validated PRISM benchmark, substantially outperforming legacy tools (IoC Searcher+whitelist 76%, AlienVault OTX 72%, VirusTotal@threshold=1 86%) and also improving downstream analyst speed (43% less annotation time) and downstream model training data quality (+6% F1). This is a single-study result from the benchmark's own authors, not yet independently replicated.

ADDED cycle 9. A second, fully independent measurement of LLM IoC extraction from real-world CTI material now exists: CyberThreat-Eval (src-0007; Microsoft Research/Microsoft/HKUST, Mar 2026), an expert-annotated benchmark built from a production CTI workflow covering 1310 IoCs, reports vanilla-LLM extraction precision of 0.8240 (GPT-4o), 0.8503 (o3-mini), 0.8846 (fine-tuned GPT-4o) and 0.6944 (fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini). Read narrowly, this establishes that a bare LLM prompted to extract indicators from real analyst-workflow material errs on roughly 1 in 6 of the indicators it emits -- materially short of the near-solved impression left by src-0003's 97.6% F1, and short of even the 86% VirusTotal@threshold=1 baseline src-0003 reports. It does NOT refute src-0003, because it measures a different system (no regex pre-filter, no human validation loop), on a different corpus, with a different metric (precision only; no recall or F1 given). See contradiction ctr-0001, opened this cycle rather than resolved either way.

ADDED cycle 9, deliberately weak status. Candidate synthesis: the reliability of mechanical IoC extraction is set mainly by the scaffolding around the model (regex pre-filtering, whitelisting, human validation) rather than by the LLM itself, which is why src-0003's scaffolded pipeline reports 97.6% F1 while src-0007's 'Vanilla LLMs' reach 0.82-0.88 precision and src-0008 finds an unscaffolded LLM recovers plaintext indicators ~100% of the time but is defeated entirely by encryption it has no tooling for. This is a plausible reading of three sources that were never designed to be compared, and no source tests it directly -- it is recorded as proposed so a later cycle can attack it, NOT as a finding. CYCLE-21 ATTACKED IT AND IT SURVIVES, BUT IT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT AT 'proposed'. What changed: the competing explanation for the same evidence -- that the src-0003/src-0007 gap is a metric artefact -- is now effectively eliminated (see the fourth candidate_resolution), which removes the main rival reading and leaves scaffolding as the live explanation. What did NOT change: no source tests this claim directly, no head-to-head exists, the corpus confound is completely unaddressed, and the 'Vanilla LLMs' heading that anchors the claim turns out to be an inference rather than a definition (see open_questions). Eliminating one rival explanation is not the same as demonstrating a causal claim about scaffolding, and promoting on that basis would be exactly the over-reach this candidate was created to resist. It stays 'proposed'.

ADDED cycle 21, and this is the cycle's substantive result. THE METRIC CONFOUND CANNOT ACCOUNT FOR THE src-0003 / src-0007 GAP, so ctr-0001 does not dissolve into an artefact of comparing an F1 with a precision. Two independent lines converge. (1) ARITHMETIC (cycle 18): for src-0007's unreported IoC recall to drag an F1 down far enough to reconcile 97.6% with a precision of 0.82-0.88, recall would have to fall in the range 0.09-0.15. (2) THE AUTHORS' OWN VERDICT (cycle 21, newly recovered from Section 4.3 of arXiv 2603.09452v1, verbatim): 'In the TI drafting stage, the extraction of IoCs is relatively robust, although improvements in recall and processing efficiency remain necessary.' A team describing their own system's IoC extraction as 'relatively robust' with recall merely needing 'improvements' is not describing recall of 0.09-0.15 -- particularly when the same paper flatly calls the TTP task, at recall 0.1414-0.2270, 'a substantial challenge'. The paper's own contrast between the two tasks puts IoC recall well above the reconciling range. SUPPORTING CONTEXT from src-0017: the omission is not a measurement limitation but a reporting decision -- the released evaluator computes recall in the same function as precision and prints it on the next line. INDEPENDENCE CAVEAT, STATED PLAINLY: both textual legs come from the same author team, and src-0017 is the same team's artefact, so this rests on ONE independent measurement plus arithmetic over src-0003's published figure, not on two independent measurements. It is an ELIMINATIVE claim -- it rules a confound out; it does not establish what the gap IS. The SYSTEM and CORPUS confounds both remain live, and ctr-0001 accordingly stays OPEN.

issues.title: Beyond raw accuracy, are LLM-generated CTI outputs consistent across repeated queries and well-calibrated in stated confidence?
open_questions: ANSWERED AT CYCLE 25 IN THE NEGATIVE, AND RESTATED AS WHAT REMAINS. src-0001's Table 6 was pulled whole for the first time at cycle 25 (caption verbatim: 'ECE and BS with gpt4o for information generation and extraction'). It is gpt4o-ONLY and complete at NINE rows -- extraction campaign/APT/CVE/attack vector, generation goals/labels/country/CVE/attack vector -- across all three paradigms; the base had stored only five of those rows. The paper reports NO ECE or Brier figure for gemini-1.5-pro-latest or mistral-large-2 ANYWHERE, so the gpt4o-specificity question cannot be settled from this source at all. WHAT REMAINS OPEN: whether the fine-tuning-can-worsen-calibration pattern is gpt4o-specific now requires a NEW measurement of proper-scoring calibration on a CTI task for a non-gpt4o model, and no such measurement exists in this base or was found by cycle 25's searches.

STILL FULLY OPEN, AND CYCLE 25 WIDENED RATHER THAN NARROWED IT. None of src-0001's 3 tested models (gpt4o, gemini-1.5-pro-latest, mistral-large-2) overlaps src-0002's (GPT-4-turbo, GPT-3.5-turbo, Gemini-1.5, LLAMA3-70B/8B) or src-0005's lists -- would the consistency/calibration findings replicate on the specific models shown to struggle with ATT&CK mapping and attribution in those benchmarks? src-0018, added this cycle, does NOT answer it either: its five models (GPT-4.1, GPT-5, GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Opus 4.5) overlap NO list in this base. So the base now has CTI-task consistency evidence on two disjoint model sets a generation apart, and zero per-model replication on any single model.

Does the multi-dimensional reliability framing (accuracy + consistency + calibration) proposed in src-0001 apply equally across the other CTI sub-tasks measured in src-0002/src-0005 (MCQ, RCM, ATE, TAA, malware analysis), or was it only measured in src-0001's own information-extraction/-generation evaluation setting?

NARROWED AT CYCLE 25, STILL OPEN. Fine-tuning and few-shot were both shown to sometimes worsen accuracy and calibration (gpt4o APT-extraction P/R 0.87->0.68 after fine-tuning; CVE-generation ECE 0.15->0.91, both re-verified exact this cycle) -- is this degradation specific to small fine-tuning dataset size / overfitting, or a general risk for CTI fine-tuning regardless of data volume? WHAT CYCLE 25 ESTABLISHED: the paper NOWHERE attributes the degradation to dataset size or overfitting (checked explicitly), so it offers no answer, and the only sentence bearing on the fine-tuning set size came back ELIDED from the fetch ('We randomly select 70% of the dataset...70% to the few-shot examples section and fine-tuning') and is therefore NOT verbatim-captured. Two concrete next steps: re-pull that split sentence verbatim, and note that the fine-tuning pool is bounded above by 350 reports either way, which makes small-data overfitting a live but unconfirmed explanation.

NEW AT CYCLE 25, AND THE CHEAPEST HIGH-VALUE ITEM ON THIS LIST. Every quantitative artefact in src-0018 is an IMAGE and none of its numbers is recoverable by this agent's fetch tooling: the table 'LLM decision consistency' (five models x {is_compromised, attack_stage} x {% of IOCs with P_o < 1, D-bar_o}), the chart 'Abstention error rates' (FDR/FNR per model), and the charts 'Selective IOC extraction performance' and 'Value assignment performance'. Two fetches instructed to answer 'IMAGE - CANNOT READ' rather than infer both did so. Until those cells are read, src-0018 supports DIRECTION only and supplies no magnitude to compare against src-0001's CI widths of 0.02 (extraction) and 0.06 (generation). Is there another route -- a companion paper, a conference talk, a PDF version, or alt-text? Cycle 25 searched for an arXiv companion by Milenkoski and Cirstea and found none.

NEW AT CYCLE 25. Does ANY source measure proper-scoring confidence calibration (ECE, Brier, reliability diagrams) on a CTI task other than src-0001? Cycle 25 ran three targeted searches and found none. Two leads were positively KILLED rather than left dangling: CTIArena (arXiv 2510.11974, Cheng/Liu/Li/Song/Gao, Virginia Tech and UC Berkeley; 9 CTI tasks, 10 models) was fetched and measures NEITHER repeat-query consistency NOR calibration/abstention, so it is not a candidate for this issue and should not be re-proposed for it; and no arXiv companion exists for src-0018. The calibration half of this issue therefore remains SINGLE-SOURCE on CTI (src-0001 alone) even though the consistency half is now two-source.

candidate_resolutions.summary: Reliability for CTI cannot be reduced to accuracy alone: on a 350-real-report evaluation, tested LLMs were both inconsistent across repeated/paraphrased queries and overconfident relative to their actual correctness, and this did not resolve with few-shot learning or fine-tuning (only partial improvement across all three paradigms tested). Exact per-model numeric scores are not yet captured in our knowledge base and are needed before this can be scored as strongly (vs. qualitatively) supported.

Full-text retrieval (cycle 3) confirms and sharpens the above with concrete numbers. The 3 tested models were gpt4o, gemini-1.5-pro-latest, and mistral-large-2. Consistency (10-re-prompt bootstrapped confidence intervals) was tight for mechanical information-extraction (max CI width 0.02) but notably wider for open-ended information-generation (max CI width 0.06). Calibration (ECE/Brier, gpt4o) was substantially worse for generation than extraction sub-tasks, and critically, fine-tuning and few-shot prompting often WORSENED both accuracy and calibration rather than uniformly 'partially improving' them -- e.g. gpt4o APT-extraction precision/recall fell from 0.87 (zero-shot) to 0.68 (fine-tuned), and CVE-generation ECE rose from 0.15 to 0.91 after fine-tuning. This refines the cycle-2 resolution: the unreliability is not just persistent across paradigms -- more training examples or fine-tuning can actively degrade both accuracy and calibration on some CTI sub-tasks.

ADDED cycle 15 by a T1 collect, status PROPOSED and deliberately not promoted -- READ THE SCOPE LIMIT BEFORE USING IT. This issue sat at score 2 from cycle 3 to cycle 15 for one reason: both candidate_resolutions above cite src-0001 and nothing else, and single-source support is a 2 by rubric. Four independent sources now measure the consistency/calibration/abstention axes on SECURITY tasks, none by src-0001's team, none on CTI material. (1) CALIBRATION: src-0013 (Siddiq/Rahman/Santos, ICSME 2026) is the first non-src-0001 source in this base reporting ECE and Brier on a security task -- GPT-4o-mini ECE 0.456-0.481, Qwen3-Coder-Next 0.408-0.421, Gemini-2.0-Flash 0.247-0.263 -- and independently reproduces src-0001's most counter-intuitive result, that an intervention meant to help can worsen calibration: moving from a controlled benchmark to a realistic repository-level setting raised ECE for every model (GPT-4o-mini 0.411->0.697, Gemini 0.161->0.721) and architectural gating helped on the controlled benchmark while degrading the realistic one. (2) INSTABILITY UNDER REPEATED IDENTICAL QUERY, src-0001's own method: src-0016 (Snyk VulnBench JS 1.0) ran each task five times with code, prompt and harness held constant and found 134/158 reference-matched findings recurred in all five runs while 80/161 unmatched findings appeared in only one of five -- a grounded-stable / volunteered-unstable split that parallels src-0001's extraction-vs-generation CI-width divide (0.02 vs 0.06). (3) PROMPT SENSITIVITY AND ABSTENTION: src-0014 (PromptAudit) fixes dataset/decoding/parsing and varies only prompting strategy, finding cross-strategy F1 ranges from 0.398 (Gemma) down to 0.103 (Mistral) and that self-consistency collapses coverage to 24.04-60.85%. (4) UNDER-REFUSAL: src-0015 (OpenSec) finds frontier IR agents over-trigger (GPT-5.2 100% containment at 82.5% FP) and locates the defect precisely -- 'the calibration gap is not in detection but in restraint' -- the same shape as src-0007's triage asymmetry. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DO. It DOES establish that consistency failure, overconfidence and under-refusal are not artefacts of one team, one paper, one model family or one evaluation harness, and it supplies the base's first abstention data. It DOES NOT replicate src-0001 on CTI: every one of the four measures a security-adjacent task (secure code generation, CVE-code vulnerability detection, JavaScript SAST review, simulated incident response), NOT IoC extraction, TTP mapping, attribution or threat-report drafting. So open_question (ii) -- would the findings replicate on src-0002's and src-0005's model lists on CTI tasks -- REMAINS FULLY OPEN, and none of the four tests a model from src-0001's, src-0002's or src-0005's lists. A T4 scoring this issue must decide explicitly whether cross-domain corroboration on the same failure mode counts toward multi-source support or whether the domain gap holds it at 2; that judgement has not been made and this entry does not make it.

SCOPE RULING, made by T2 at cycle 16 and recorded here so that no future cycle re-litigates it. THE QUESTION cycle 15's T1 raised and correctly refused to answer: it added four independent sources (src-0013, src-0014, src-0015, src-0016) measuring consistency, calibration and abstention on SECURITY tasks, and asked whether cross-domain corroboration of the same failure mode counts toward multi-source support for this issue, or whether the domain gap holds it at single-source. THE RULING IS THAT THE DOMAIN GAP HOLDS. This issue's scope stays anchored to CTI, and the two candidate_resolutions above -- the only ones making a claim about CTI material -- remain single-source (src-0001) for scoring purposes. REASONING, three grounds. (a) Every one of the four measures a security-ADJACENT task -- secure code generation, CVE-code vulnerability detection, JavaScript SAST review, simulated incident response -- and none measures IoC extraction, TTP mapping, attribution or threat-report drafting, which are the tasks this topic is scoped to. (b) Not one tests a model from src-0001's, src-0002's or src-0005's lists; the model overlap is empty, so open_questions (i) and (ii) are untouched by them and must NOT be marked answered. (c) This base's own precedent for admitting a security-adjacent source is src-0008 (JavaScript obfuscation), which was admitted WITH an explicit scope gap and was never treated as a replication of the CTI work; ruling the other way here would retroactively change what that precedent meant. WHAT IS NEVERTHELESS ESTABLISHED, and it is not nothing: the MECHANISM -- output instability under identical or perturbed input, systematic overconfidence, and under-refusal -- is robust across four unrelated teams, four methods, four corpora and roughly fifteen models, so it is not an artefact of one paper, one team or one model family; and two of src-0001's most fragile-looking sub-findings are independently echoed by different mechanisms (an intervention intended to help WORSENING calibration: src-0013's repository-level ECE rising 0.411 to 0.697 for GPT-4o-mini and 0.161 to 0.721 for Gemini-2.0-Flash, and src-0014's adaptive-CoT reducing recall for every model, e.g. Gemma 0.420 to 0.057; and GROUNDED-OUTPUT-STABLE versus VOLUNTEERED-OUTPUT-UNSTABLE: src-0016's 134 of 158 reference-matched findings recurring in all five identical repetitions against 80 of 161 unmatched findings appearing in only one of five, paralleling src-0001's extraction-vs-generation CI widths of 0.02 vs 0.06). That is a claim about SECURITY-TASK LLM RELIABILITY GENERALLY. It is held here as context for the CTI claim, not as support for it. CONSEQUENCE FOR A T4: score this issue on its CTI candidates. A T4 may overrule this scope ruling, but if it does it must say so explicitly and give its reason -- what it must not do is silently count the four as multi-source support for a CTI claim. NO SCORE IS SET HERE; scoring is T4's work and this entry deliberately does not perform it. TWO THINGS REMAIN UNCHANGED AND SHOULD NOT BE FORGOTTEN: this base still has no non-src-0001 source measuring consistency AND calibration together, and per carry-forward [20] src-0013's and src-0014's numbers are single-pass fetches whose results tables have never been pulled whole, with src-0013 additionally carrying an unreconciled internal discrepancy (False Trust for GPT-4o-mini given as 33.9% in one section and as rising from 16.9% to 83.2% in another) -- those two figures must not be quoted together until a G2 pulls that table.

ADDED AND PROMOTED TO SUPPORTED BY CYCLE 25's T3. THE CTI-DOMAIN SINGLE-SOURCE BLOCKER IS BROKEN, BUT FOR THE CONSISTENCY HALF ONLY -- read the split below before scoring. THE CLAIM: on CTI material specifically, LLM outputs are NOT stable across repeated identical queries, and this is now measured by two teams with nothing in common. (1) src-0001 (Mezzi, Massacci, Tuma; ARES 2025, peer-reviewed -- see the cycle-25 note appended to that source, the base had wrongly carried it as an unreviewed preprint since cycle 1): 350 real threat-intelligence reports, 3 models, ten re-prompts per input with bootstrapped CIs, max CI width 0.02 for information extraction and 0.06 for information generation. The cycle-25 whole-table pull recovered the protocol sentence verbatim -- 'we re-prompt each LLM ten times on the same input, with temperature=0 and the same seed to guarantee maximum determinism' -- so the measured spread is RESIDUAL NON-DETERMINISM UNDER MAXIMAL DETERMINISM SETTINGS, which strengthens the finding. (2) src-0018 (Milenkoski and Cirstea, SentinelLabs, 9 March 2026): selective IOC/hash/playbook extraction from narrative threat reports, ground truth of 343 atomic IOCs and 1859 labeled contextual-attribute instances, five current-generation models, 'repeated executions of each evaluation experiment' under 'identical conditions', with two purpose-built decision-consistency metrics (share of IOCs receiving two or more different values for one attribute across runs; average mode-based observed disagreement). INDEPENDENCE IS CLEAN: no shared author, academia vs industry lab, different corpora, model sets a full generation apart and disjoint, and src-0018 does not cite src-0001. This clears the cycle-16 scope ruling on its own terms rather than overturning it -- src-0018 is CTI proper (IOC extraction from threat reports), not a security-adjacent task, so no cross-domain generalisation is being asserted. TWO LIMITS A T4 MUST HOLD ONTO. (a) src-0018 SUPPLIES NO NUMBERS: all four of its quantitative artefacts are images this agent cannot read, so the corroboration is of DIRECTION AND EXISTENCE only, and no magnitude may be compared with src-0001's CI widths. (b) THE CALIBRATION HALF IS UNTOUCHED: src-0018 measures ABSTENTION errors (FDR/FNR over an explicit None class), which is a restraint construct and NOT ECE/Brier -- the same non-pooling rule already recorded for src-0015. Proper-scoring calibration on CTI remains src-0001-only, gpt4o-only, nine table rows. SO THE HONEST SCORING POSITION IS SPLIT: consistency-on-CTI is now two-source and qualitative-plus-quantitative; calibration-on-CTI is still one-source. This issue's title asks both.

ADDED BY CYCLE 25's T3 (G2 by-product, promoted because it is verified directly against the source's own printed table). WHAT src-0001's TABLE 6 ACTUALLY SHOWS, now that it has been pulled whole for the first time in 25 cycles. Caption verbatim: 'ECE and BS with gpt4o for information generation and extraction.' Nine rows, gpt4o only, three paradigms, ECE and BS. Extraction, zero-shot | few-shot | fine-tuning ECE: campaign 0.25 | 0.26 | 0.48; APT 0.16 | 0.17 | 0.25; CVE 0.28 | 0.35 | 0.18; attack vector 0.13 | 0.19 | 0.27. Generation, same order: goals 0.13 | 0.04 | 0.08; labels 0.45 | 0.57 | 0.48; country 0.19 | 0.38 | 0.35; CVE 0.15 | 0.13 | 0.91; attack vector 0.47 | 0.48 | 0.87. THREE CONSEQUENCES. (i) The five cells this base had stored are all EXACT; the base had simply never held the other four rows or the few-shot column. (ii) The generation-is-worse-calibrated-than-extraction framing carried in candidate_resolutions 1 and 2 above and in src-0001's key_claims[4] DOES NOT HOLD ROW-WISE AT ZERO-SHOT -- generation goals 0.13, CVE 0.15 and country 0.19 are all better calibrated than extraction campaign 0.25 and extraction CVE 0.28, and the framing's own worked example (CVE generation 0.15) beats its extraction counterpart (0.28). What holds is a mean gap that is small at zero-shot (generation 0.278 vs extraction 0.205) and large after fine-tuning (0.538 vs 0.295), driven almost entirely by two fine-tuned generation rows. Those four means are DERIVED BY THIS AGENT from the printed cells and are NOT printed in the paper. Contradiction ctr-0003 is opened for this; nothing above has been rewritten. (iii) The strongest surviving version of the fine-tuning finding is not about extraction vs generation at all but about DIRECTION OF CHANGE: relative to zero-shot, fine-tuning WORSENED ECE on 7 of the 9 rows and WORSENED BS on the same 7 (derived by cell-by-cell comparison, not printed), improving only extraction CVE (ECE 0.28->0.18, BS 0.32->0.21) and generation goals (ECE 0.13->0.08, BS 0.14->0.05) -- so 'fine-tuning does not reliably improve calibration and sometimes destroys it' is well supported, whereas 'generation is markedly worse than extraction' is not, at least not before fine-tuning.

issues.title: How large is the gap between 'plausible-sounding' and 'factually correct' LLM threat-actor attribution?
open_questions: REWRITTEN cycle 28 (T3). THE QUESTION AS PREVIOUSLY POSED IS MALFORMED AND IS RETIRED, NOT DELETED; the old wording asked whether 'the plausible-vs-correct gap' measured on 2024-era models narrows for later models, and ctr-0002 established that that gap is TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION -- CTIBench defines Plausible Accuracy as 'the fraction of correct and plausible answers combined', so it contains Correct Accuracy and there is no empirical quantity there to narrow. THE WELL-POSED REPLACEMENT: does CTIBench's own INCORRECT bucket -- the hallucination-inclusive one, defined verbatim as 'when the LLM misattributes the threat actor due to misjudgment, hallucination, or spurious correlation', numerically equal to 100 minus Plausible Accuracy and standing at 14 / 38 / 26 / 20 / 64 percent for GPT-4-turbo / GPT-3.5-turbo / Gemini-1.5 / LLAMA3-70B / LLAMA3-8B (DERIVED BY SUBTRACTION FROM TABLE 1, NOT PRINTED IN THE PAPER) -- fall for post-2024 models? STATUS: NO SOURCE IN THIS BASE ANSWERS IT, and cycle 28 confirms the previous cycle's diagnosis rather than improving on it. src-0007's 1-5 'Content: Threat Actor' rubric is the only later-generation threat-actor measurement here and it reports a graded quality score, not a correct / underdetermined-but-related / outright-wrong partition, so it cannot be converted into this quantity at any exchange rate. What is missing is any source that partitions post-2024 attribution outputs into those three buckets, or that reports an outright-misattribution rate for a post-2024 model. This is the highest-value collection target for this issue; the next T1 is cycle 43, so the realistic route is a T3 with search budget.

NOT WORKED AT CYCLE 28 -- HONEST DEFERRAL, recorded so no successor assumes it was checked. THE QUESTION, unchanged: is attribution error correlated with how well-documented a threat actor group is (e.g. major APTs with abundant public reporting vs. obscure/emerging groups)? Cycle 28's budget went to ctr-0002's three-step resolution path and to a G2 on src-0018, and this question was not touched. NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT, from inspection of the base rather than from a fetch: no source here publishes a per-report or per-actor breakdown of attribution outcomes -- src-0002's CTI-TAA result is 50 reports reported only as aggregate percentages in Table 1, and src-0007's 'Content: Threat Actor' rubric is likewise a corpus aggregate -- so the question cannot be answered from stored values and needs new material. The cheapest untried route is CTIBench's own released dataset/evaluation artefact, which would carry per-report ground truth; that is the same route that worked for src-0007 at cycle 21 (src-0017) and no cycle has looked for CTIBench's equivalent.

ANSWERED AT CYCLE 28 (T3), after ten cycles in which it was merely articulated. THE QUESTION WAS: did ENISA's APT29/'Midnight Blizzard' naming-convention hallucination (src-0004) contribute to, or correlate with, the kind of plausible-but-wrong attribution measured quantitatively in src-0002, or is it a distinct hallucination sub-type (citation/naming fabrication vs. attribution judgment)? THE ANSWER IS: DISTINCT SUB-TYPE. THE DECIDING ARGUMENT COMES FROM src-0002'S OWN SCORING RULE, already stored verbatim in this base: 'To further ensure accuracy, we manually verify each LLM response to account for the multiple aliases that threat actors often use.' CTI-TAA SCORES AN ALIAS AS CORRECT -- its 'correct answer' bucket is defined as 'when the LLM accurately identifies the threat actor or one of its aliases'. APT29 and Midnight Blizzard are two names for one group, and the ENISA passage names the right group; its error is the claim about WHICH VENDOR USES WHICH NAME, i.e. a false statement about naming provenance, not a false statement about who conducted the activity. Under CTI-TAA's own rule the ENISA sentence would be scored CORRECT. The ENISA defect is therefore INVISIBLE TO THE MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT this issue's quantified leg rests on, and the two cannot be instances of one measured phenomenon. Two corroborating considerations, neither load-bearing: the same ENISA report's other documented defect is 26 of 492 incorrect footnotes, a citation-validity failure of exactly the kind src-0011 (GhostCite) and src-0012 (EY Canada) measure; and src-0004 attaches no accuracy or confidence measurement of any kind to the passage. CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED AGAINST THIS ISSUE'S OWN INTEREST: src-0004's evidential home is institutional-incident-real-world-impact, and it must not be counted as an independent second source for THIS issue's central claim -- which is why the primary candidate below now cites src-0002 alone, where it previously cited src-0002 and src-0004. RESIDUAL, GENUINELY OPEN AND NOT TO BE ASSERTED EITHER WAY: whether the two sub-types share an upstream generative cause (both being ungrounded production of a specific-looking fact) is a mechanism question that no source in this base tests.

candidate_resolutions.summary: REWRITTEN AT CYCLE 28 (T3), executing step (i) of ctr-0002's resolution path. THE 86-VS-52 FRAMING IS RETIRED, NOT REPAIRED. The old text of this candidate said 'every one of the 5 tested models' plausible-sounding attribution rate substantially exceeds its correct attribution rate (e.g. GPT-4-turbo: 86% plausible vs 52% correct; Gemini-1.5: 74% vs 38%)'; CTIBench defines Plausible Accuracy as 'the fraction of correct and plausible answers combined', so it CONTAINS Correct Accuracy and that inequality is true by construction for every model on every dataset. It evidenced nothing and is withdrawn. WHAT REPLACES IT. CTI-TAA partitions each response into three buckets, verbatim: 'correct answer (when the LLM accurately identifies the threat actor or one of its aliases), plausible answer (when the threat report lacks sufficient details to pinpoint the answer, but the LLM provides a plausible or related threat actor within a similar group), and incorrect answer (when the LLM misattributes the threat actor due to misjudgment, hallucination, or spurious correlation)'. The THIRD bucket is the paper's own hallucination-inclusive misattribution rate and equals 100 minus Plausible Accuracy: GPT-4-turbo 14%, GPT-3.5-turbo 38%, Gemini-1.5 26%, LLAMA3-70B 20%, LLAMA3-8B 64%, over 50 real threat reports, with the authors stating that they 'manually verify each LLM response to account for the multiple aliases that threat actors often use'. THOSE FIVE VALUES ARE DERIVED BY SUBTRACTION FROM TABLE 1 BY THIS AGENT AND ARE NOT PRINTED ANYWHERE IN THE PAPER; every cell they are derived from was re-verified EXACT against Table 1 by two independent fetches at cycle 23, and the ChatGPT-4 row was re-confirmed a third time at cycle 28. THE FINDING: outright misattribution of the threat actor is common in 2024-era models, from roughly one report in seven for the best model to nearly two in three for the weakest, on real reports scored with alias tolerance. WHAT THIS CANDIDATE DOES NOT CLAIM, and the distinction is the whole point of this issue: src-0002 measures WRONGNESS, NOT CONFIDENCE. It records no verbalised confidence, no hedging rate, no calibration metric and no reader-facing plausibility judgement, and no sentence in the paper interprets the correct-versus-plausible gap. Its 'plausible' bucket is scoped to UNDERDETERMINED INPUT answered with a related actor from a similar group -- arguably reasonable behaviour under ambiguity -- and is explicitly NOT its hallucination bucket. The string 'plausible-sounding' does not occur in the paper, though this state presented it in scare quotes for 27 cycles. This candidate is therefore supported as an ATTRIBUTION-ERROR-RATE finding and supplies no support whatever for the 'confident' half of this issue's title. src-0004 has been REMOVED from this candidate's evidence: see open_question[2], answered this cycle, which finds the ENISA error to be a distinct sub-type invisible to CTI-TAA's scoring rule.

THE SURVEY FINDING, which is the substance of the (b) half: NO SOURCE IN THIS KNOWLEDGE BASE MEASURES EXPRESSED CONFIDENCE ON THREAT-ACTOR ATTRIBUTION. src-0002 partitions outputs by correctness only and records no confidence construct of any kind (its metric section defines accuracy for CTI-MCQ/CTI-RCM, MAD for CTI-VSP, F1 for CTI-ATE, and the three-bucket partition for CTI-TAA -- nothing else). src-0007's 'Content: Threat Actor' block is an LLM-judged 1-5 quality rubric (Relevance / Accuracy / Attribution) whose absolute level is uninterpretable and which grades attribution QUALITY, not how confidently the model asserts it. src-0004 is a single published passage with no measurement attached at all. CONSEQUENCE: this issue's titular quantity, the gap between plausible-SOUNDING and factually correct attribution, IS UNMEASURED BY EVERY SOURCE IT CITES. That is a finding about the evidence, not a claim about the world -- it does not show the gap is small or absent, it shows that nobody in this base has measured it, and no cycle may treat attribution error rates as a proxy for it. issues.title: Is 'AI-generated CTI reliability' a single property, or does it vary sharply by task type (mechanical extraction vs. open-ended reasoning)?
open_questions: SPLIT NOTE (cycle 16, T2, discharging carry-forward [1] after it was carried unactioned for nine consecutive cycles). This issue now covers ONLY the narrow claim: that AI-generated CTI reliability varies sharply by sub-task rather than being a single uniform property. The SPECIFIC ORDINAL AXIS ('mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation'), together with the cycle-2 proposed cross-source synthesis that carried it and the open question about whether a better explanatory variable exists, was MOVED VERBATIM to the new issue 'extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis'. The reason for the split is that the two claims have very different evidential status and were sharing one issue and one candidate_resolution from cycle 2 to cycle 15, which is exactly why no T4 could score either honestly: the narrow claim has five independent supporting sources (src-0001, src-0002, src-0006, src-0007, and now src-0013 on the calibration axis) while the ordinal axis is actively disputed between src-0006 and src-0007. Do NOT re-merge them.

src-0006's causal-intervention mitigations raised an attribution-adjacent task (Threat Actor Linking) by only +0.055 accuracy, a much smaller gain than LANCE's ~72-86%->97.6% F1 jump on IoC extraction (src-0003) -- but the two are not a controlled comparison (different tasks, metrics, mitigation types: automated retrieval/inference intervention vs. human-in-the-loop regex+LLM pipeline). No source yet tests a LANCE-style human-validated pipeline specifically on ATT&CK mapping or attribution; a search this cycle for such a study (and for RAM/src-2502.02337, an automated non-human-in-the-loop ATT&CK mapper) found none. Does human-in-the-loop validation specifically (not just any targeted mitigation) transfer to reasoning-heavy tasks, and if so how much of the IoC-extraction gain would it recover?

Since src-0003's strong result is single-study/in-house, would the task-dependence conclusion survive an independent replication showing a smaller IoC-extraction advantage? A cycle-6 search for independent LANCE/PRISM replication or critique found none published yet.

candidate_resolutions.summary: The core, narrower claim -- that AI-generated CTI reliability is genuinely task-dependent rather than a single uniform property -- is now supported, not just proposed: src-0006 (cycle 6) directly measures reliability across multiple distinct CTI sub-tasks within one consistent study design (rather than only via cross-benchmark synthesis across different teams/models) and finds F1/AUC ranging roughly 0.20-0.90 by specific sub-task, corroborating the cross-study pattern already visible in src-0001/0002/0003/0005. However, the SPECIFIC ordinal axis proposed above (mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation) is not confirmed by this evidence and is likely too coarse: src-0006 found its failure patterns cut across all 4 CTI pipeline stages it defines, including extraction/contextualization-type tasks, rather than concentrating in 'reasoning' stages. So: task-dependence itself = supported; the specific extraction-vs-reasoning explanatory axis = open, and now positively questioned rather than merely unverified.

ADDED cycle 16 by T2 at the split. Two further within-study measurements strengthen the NARROW claim -- that CTI reliability varies sharply by sub-task rather than being one uniform property -- and both are of the strongest available kind, holding team, corpus, models and harness constant and varying only the sub-task. (1) src-0007: on one expert-annotated corpus drawn from a real company's CTI workflow, the same four models reach IoC-extraction precision 0.8240-0.8846 while scoring 0.2787/0.2270 (GPT-4o) and 0.3480/0.1759 (o3-mini) precision/recall on MITRE ATT&CK TTP identification, and GPT-4o scores 1.140 out of 5 on the threat-actor Attribution rubric against 3.612 out of 5 for root-cause content in the same table -- roughly a 3x spread across sub-tasks with everything else held constant. (2) src-0013 extends task-dependence to a NEW AXIS that no prior source in this base had tested: reliability varies by sub-task not only in accuracy but in CALIBRATION. Within one study, functional calibration is consistently worse than security calibration for every model tested (delta ECE -0.15/-0.16 GPT-4o-mini, -0.26/-0.27 Gemini-2.0-Flash, -0.52/-0.53 Qwen3-Coder-Next). SCOPE LIMIT ON (2), do not strip it: src-0013 measures secure code generation, not CTI, so it corroborates the SHAPE of task-dependence on a security-adjacent task rather than replicating it on CTI material -- see the cycle-16 scope ruling recorded in 'consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode', which declines to treat security-adjacent corroboration as CTI multi-source support. PROVENANCE ASYMMETRY: src-0007's figures were re-verified verbatim by cycle 15's G2 and are exact to four decimal places; src-0013's are single-pass fetches whose results tables have never been pulled whole (carry-forward [20]). This candidate supports TASK-DEPENDENCE ONLY and deliberately takes no position on the ordinal ranking of sub-tasks, which was moved out of this issue to 'extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis' at the cycle-16 split.

issues.title: Is there a valid ordinal difficulty ranking across CTI sub-tasks (mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation), or is the extraction-vs-reasoning binary too coarse to explain where reliability breaks down?
open_questions: CYCLE-18 HEADLINE, and it changes what this issue is asking. The commensurable measurement that the 'WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY SETTLE THIS' question below demanded ALREADY EXISTS IN THIS KNOWLEDGE BASE and has since cycle 6: src-0006's Table 2 contains nine rows all reported in F1, over ONE corpus and ONE 15-model set (printed column order G5, Go4, CLD, GEM, LL70, MIX, QWN, GRK, FSC, CB0, ZYS, LLY, CBS, SPT, DHT; 8 general-purpose then 7 cybersecurity-specialised), spanning both ends of the proposed ordering. Restricted to those nine rows the yardstick does not change between sub-tasks, which is exactly the property src-0007 lacks. The table was pulled whole and recomputed at cycle 17, then pulled again from a second URL form and recomputed independently at cycle 18 -- cycle 17's state edits were reverted by the validator, so cycle 18 is the first time this finding has landed. THE ORDERING IS NOT REPRODUCED. Mean F1 across all 15 models, Contextualization ('extraction') stage: IOC Normalization 0.656, Affected Systems 0.650, Attack Infrastructure 0.631, Malware Family Mapping 0.607, stage mean 0.636. Attribution ('reasoning') stage: TTP Extraction 0.673, Infrastructure Reuse 0.612, Relation Graph Building 0.610, False Flag Detection 0.511, stage mean 0.602. Stage gap 0.034 F1 -- about one fifth of the within-Attribution spread (0.511-0.673) and about one eighth of the mean between-model spread on a single task (0.272). The single BEST task in the whole commensurable subset is TTP Extraction at 0.673, an Attribution-stage task, outscoring every Contextualization task including IOC Normalization: the predicted ordering is not merely weak, it is locally inverted at its strongest predicted point. WHAT IS NOW OPEN: (a) does a 0.034 stage gap survive a SECOND commensurable multi-sub-task study; (b) is 0.034 distinguishable from zero at all, given that src-0006 reports no confidence intervals, no seeds and no repeat runs, so this issue cannot presently attach an uncertainty to its own headline number; (c) src-0006's stage labels are the paper's own four-stage pipeline taxonomy and 'Contextualization' is a looser construct than 'mechanical extraction', so a future cycle should test whether re-labelling the nine tasks by output-label-space size rather than by pipeline stage produces a cleaner split.

NEW cycle 18, and it is the strongest replacement hypothesis on the table. On the same nine-row commensurable F1 subset of src-0006's Table 2, the mean BETWEEN-MODEL range within a task is 0.272 (Affected Systems 0.464, False Flag Detection 0.393, Attack Infrastructure 0.371, Patch Recommendation 0.276, TTP Extraction 0.273, Infrastructure Reuse 0.226, Malware Family Mapping 0.155, Relation Graph Building 0.155, IOC Normalization 0.132) and the mean BETWEEN-TASK range within a model is 0.263 (from 0.171 for ZYS up to 0.404 for LL70 and 0.403 for LLY). EQUAL TO WITHIN 0.009. That answers the last inherited open_question below in the affirmative and mis-specifies the axis: task identity is not the dominant explanatory variable, model identity is at least its equal. A further and weaker signal points at CORPUS identity: the same nominal sub-task, ATT&CK TTP mapping, scores F1 0.478-0.751 in src-0006 but a derived F1 of 0.157-0.250 in src-0007 -- a shift of roughly 0.4 on ONE task, larger than any between-task gap either paper reports. That comparison is uncontrolled (task definition, model set, publication year and metric decomposition all differ at once) and is recorded as a lead, not a result. STILL OPEN: is there any study that varies task while holding model fixed and varies model while holding task fixed, reporting variance components rather than leaving them to a reader's arithmetic? No source in this base does.

NEW cycle 18, and it is a caveat on this issue's own headline evidence rather than a question about CTI. Four of the nine commensurable F1 rows in src-0006's Table 2 -- IOC Normalization, Malware Family Mapping, Relation Graph Building, Infrastructure Reuse -- are STRICTLY MONOTONE DECREASING across all eight general-purpose model columns in exactly the printed column order, with unusually smooth decrements. The cycle-18 headline is deliberately robust to it: dropping all four monotone rows leaves Contextualization 0.641 against Attribution 0.592, gap 0.049, same direction, TTP Extraction still the highest single task. STATUS CHANGED FROM 'proposed' TO 'rejected'.
